newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Dutch ING profits as banking shines.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dutch ING profits as banking shines.

text.p: Dutch financial services giant ING Groep NV on Thursday delivered a 24 percent increase in nine month net profit, despite hefty provisions, as banking continued to outpace its larger insurance operations for growth.
ING also forecast a rise in full year earnings per share.
A net profit of 2.34 billion guilders ($1.4 billion), up from 1.88 billion a year earlier, agreed with most forecasts and the group's shares regained some of their earlier losses.
"ING Group's results showed a continued strong growth in the first nine months of 1996," the group said.

It made provisions totalling 275 million guilders for information technology, costs associated with the introduction of the euro single currency and the year 2000, and enhanced marketing efforts and reorganisations within insurance.
Pre-tax profits from banking rose 26.9 percent to 1.62 billion guilders for the nine month period while insurance profits increased 16.0 percent to 1.72 billion.
In banking, net interest results rose 13.2 percent, commission income by 35.1 percent and results from financial transactions, or trading, by 52.7 percent.
Securities trading income was helped by favourable markets and a relatively low comparison due to the aftermath of the 1995 Mexican peso crisis.
Barings, the London-based investment bank which ING bought last year after it collapsed from derivatives trading losses, contributed to a rise in commission income and in costs.
But ING did not give separate results for the high profile acquisition, as it is now part of the ING Barings investment banking division.

In insurance, life profits rose 14.8 percent, helped by stronger results from the Netherlands, Hungary and Australia, while the 16.3 percent growth in non-life results flowed from sharply improved results in the Netherlands and Australia.
The comparative period in 1995 was marred by a 60 million guilder charge related to Hurricane Luis in the Caribbean, while the 1996 result was affected by a severe winter and U.S. storms.
Within non-life, fire operations remained loss making due to U.S. weather conditions, but motor results showed a considerable improvement in almost all areas.
ING also foresaw a strong full year result.

It said: "Despite the increase in share capital through stock dividends and the conversion of warrants, ING expects, on the basis of the nine month result, that net profits per share over the whole of 1996 will be clearly higher compared to 1995."
Net profit in 1995 was 2.65 billion guilders, or 9.60 guilders per share, but since then the group has increased the number of shares on issue through a 2.5-for-one share split.
Analysts were generally positive about the results and said they may raise their profit forecasts for the full year.
"The insurance and the banking activities showed healthy growth, in spite of substantial extra costs," said Heini Hakker at BZW in Amsterdam.
James Alexander of London-based Kleinwort Benson said: "We weren't expecting banking to be quite as good as it was."
ING shares, which weakened ahead of and just after the result, were trading at 58.80 guilders at 1410 GMT, down 20 cents on the previous close but off the day's low of 57.20.
($ = 1.68 Dutch guilders)
